title: Salmon, Broccoli and Rice Salad
description: By Ashley Lonsdale (NYT): The heartbeat of this hearty salad is the sweet, oven-roasted edges of broccoli florets and red onion wedges. Chewy bits of steamed rice, hunks of roasted salmon and a salty, savory anchovy-lemon dressing make it much more of a dinner than a side dish. The broccoli can also be traded for other cruciferous vegetables like cabbage, cauliflower or brussels sprouts if the mood strikes.
ingredients: 1 (1-pound) salmon fillet, skin on or off
¼ cup extra-virgin olive oil, divided
Salt and freshly ground black pepper
1 ½ pounds broccoli crowns, trimmed, cut into cut into 1- to 1 ½-inch pieces
1 large red onion, sliced into thick wedges
4 tablespoons fresh lemon juice, from 1 to 2 lemons
2 large handfuls watercress or baby arugula (about 2 ounces)
directions: Rub the salmon fillet with 1 tablespoon olive oil and season with salt and pepper on all sides.

Rinse the rice until water runs clear. In a small lidded saucepan, combine the rice, 1 ¼ cups water and 1 tablespoon olive oil. Season the water to taste with salt and bring to a boil over high heat. Cover and reduce to a gentle simmer over medium-low and cook for 12 to 15 minutes, until the rice is plumped. Remove from heat and let rest, covered, for 5 minutes.

Meanwhile, on a large sheet pan, toss the broccoli, red onion and remaining 2 tablespoons olive oil. Season generously with salt and pepper. Roast in the oven for 15 or so, tossing once, until tender-crisp and lightly browned.
After the first 5 minutes, add the salmon fillet skin side down (if present) to the same pan (or another pan) and roast until just cooked through, about 10 minutes.
While the salmon roasts, add the lemon juice, mustard and anchovies to a large salad bowl and mix well. Season with salt and pepper to taste.
When the oven time is up, add the broccoli mixture and cooked rice to the dressing bowl and toss lightly.
Flake the salmon (discarding any skin) and add to the bowl. Fold in three-fourths of the watercress. Top with the remaining watercress and serve.
